questions.question:
The Bar Graph shows the Production and Sales of Mobile handsets of various companies A, B, C, D, E & F in a month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58d3211c61b55dee313e5bc02dc79e63c9eee380a55a0d0db24b7796fd16ee7a.png] 

The total units sold by Companies A, B and C together is approximately what per cent of the total units produced by Companies A, B and C together (correct to nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
The total units sold by Companies A, B and C together = 650 + 300 + 150 = 1100

The total units produced by Companies A, B and C together = 900 + 700 + 300 = 1900

Let the required percentage be x%

According to question,

1100 = x% × 1900

⇒ 1100 = x/100 × 1900

⇒ x = 1100/19

∴ The required percentage is 58%

Which Company had the highest percentage of sale with respect to its production?
questions.solution:
The sale of company A with respect to its production = 650/900 = 13/18

The sale of company B with respect to its production = 300/700 = 3/7

The sale of company C with respect to its production = 150/300 = 1/2

The sale of company D with respect to its production = 450/850 = 9/17

The sale of company E with respect to its production = 330/550 = 3/5

After comparing the above ratio, we get 13/18 is the greatest of all

∴ The sale of company A is highest with respect to its production.

questions.question: On selling an article for Rs. 2400 a trader earns 25% profit. If he had sold it for Rs. 2160, then what was his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of the article be Rs. X

According to question,

X × 125% = 2400

⇒ X × 5/4 = 2400

⇒ X = 1920

⇒ The cost price is Rs. 1920

Since, new selling price = Rs. 2160 and it is greater than 1920 (cost price of article)

⇒ Profit percentage = [(2160 – 1920)/1920] × 100

∴ Profit percentage is 25/2%

questions.question: The mode of 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10 is:
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

The mode is the value that appears **most frequently** in a data set.

**Explanation:**

Given, 2 occurs two times

⇒ 3 occurs two times

⇒ 5 occurs three times

⇒ 7 occurs one times

⇒ 8 occurs two times

⇒ 9 occurs one times

⇒ 10 occurs one times

**∴ The mode of this data is 5**

questions.question: HCF and LCM of two numbers p and q are A and B respectively, if A + B = p + q, then the value of A³ + B³ is:
questions.solution:
Since, we know that L.C.M × H.C.F = product of numbers

So, A × B = p × q ----(i)

And, it is given that A + B = p + q ----(ii)

Since, we also know that

A³ + B³ = (A + B)[(A + B)² – 3AB]

⇒ A³ + B³ = p + q [(p + q)² – 3pq]

∴ A³ + B³ = p³ + q³

questions.question: Two classes M and N have average marks 25 and 40 respectively. The overall average obtained is 30. The ratio of the students in the class M and N is:
questions.solution:
Let the number of students in two classes M and N are x and y respectively.

According to question,

The sum of marks obtained by all students in class M = 25x

And, the sum of marks obtained by all students in class N = 40y

⇒ The total marks obtained by all the students of both class = (25x + 40y)

⇒ The average marks obtained by all students of both class = (25x + 40y)/(x + y)

Again, according to question

(25x + 40y)/(x + y) = 30

⇒ 25x + 40y = 30x + 30y

⇒ 10y = 5x

⇒ x : y = 2 : 1

∴ The ratio of number of students of class M and class N are in the ratio 2 : 1

questions.question: If the length of a side of the square is equal to that of the diameter of a circle, then the ratio of the area of the square and that of the circle is: ( {{{pi}} = {{}}frac{{22}}{7}} )
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the length of the side of the square be a unit

So, the diameter of the circle is a unit.

The ratio of the circle is a/2 unit

The required ratio = a² : π(a/2)² = a² : 22/7 × a²/4 = 28 : 22

**∴ The ratio of the area of the square to the area of the circle is 14 : 11**

questions.question: a and b are two numbers such that their mean proportion is 6 and third proportion is 48. What is the value of a and b?
questions.solution:
Mean proportion of a and b = √ab

But it is given that, the mean proportion is 6

So, √ab = 6

⇒ ab = 36 ----(i)

And, third proportion of a and b = b²/a

But it is given that, the third proportion is 48

So, b²/a = 48 ----(ii)

On putting the value of a from (ii) in (i), we get

b³ = 48 × 36

⇒ b = 12

Now, from (i)

12 × a = 36

⇒ a = 3

∴ The value of a and b are 3 and 12 respectively.

questions.question: Daily ticket of a metro train costs Rs. 120 and Monthly pass costs Rs. 3276. If Sohan buys the Monthly pass and travels for 30 days in a month then what Percentage does the save?
questions.solution:
Given, monthly pass = Rs. 3276

And, daily ticket cost = Rs. 120

If he travels on daily basis, then the monthly cost of Sohan will be Rs. 120 × 30

⇒ Rs. 3600

⇒ The saving percentage of Sohan = (3600 – 3276)/3600 × 100%

∴ The saving percentage of Sohan is 9%

questions.question: A bag contains the amount of Rs. 25.8 in the form of 1 rupee, 50 paisa and 10 paisa coins and are in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 3. How many 50 paisa coins are there in the bag?
questions.solution:
Let the number of 1 rupee, 50 paisa, and 10 paisa coins are 3x, 2x and 3x respectively

Now, according to question

3x × 1 + 2x × 50/100 + 3x × 10/100 = 25.8

⇒ 3x + x + 3x/10 = 25.8

⇒ 43x/10 = 25.8

⇒ x = 6

∴ The number of 50 paisa coins is = 6 × 2 = 12

questions.question: At what percent per annum will Rs. 6000 amounts to Rs. 7986 in 3 years, if the interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Let the rate percentage be R% per annum

According to question,

7986 = 6000 (1 + R/100)³

⇒ (1 + R/100)³ = 7986/6000

⇒ (1 + R/100)³ = 1331/1000

⇒ (1 + R/100) = (1331/1000)¹/³

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 11/10

⇒ R/100 = 1/10

∴ The rate percent per annum is 10%

questions.question: X takes 10 days less than the time taken by Y to finish a piece of work. X and Y together can do it in 12 days. In how many days Y-alone can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Let the time taken by Y to finish the work be a days

⇒ The time taken by X to finish the work is (a – 10) days

⇒ The work done by Y in 1 day = 1/a

And, the work done by X in 1 day = 1/(a – 10)

According to question,

1/a + 1/(a – 10) = 1/12

⇒ (2a – 10)/(a² – 10a) = 1/12

⇒ a² – 10a = 24a – 120

⇒ a² – 34a + 120 = 0

⇒ (a – 30) (a – 4) = 0

So, a = 30 or a = 4 (which is not possible)

∴ Y can alone finish the work in 30 days
